name: 009_double_dash_passes_option_to_command.sh
exercises: flags/examples: -- delimits end of sudo options
expected: token after -- is passed to the command, not parsed by sudo
manpage_quote: The -- is used to delimit the end of the sudo options.  Subsequent options are passed to the command.

name: 010_run_command_exit_status_passthrough.sh
expected: sudo exits with the command's exit status (7)
manpage_quote: Upon successful execution of a command, the exit status from sudo will be the exit status of the program that was executed.

name: 011_u_numeric_uid_hash.sh
expected: sudo -u #0 runs the command with UID 0
manpage_quote: The user may be either a user name or a numeric user-ID (UID) prefixed with the ‘#’ character (e.g., ‘#0’ for UID 0).

name: 012_g_numeric_gid_hash.sh
exercises: flags/identity: -g numeric GID via '#' prefix sets primary group
expected: sudo -g #0 sets the command's primary group to GID 0
manpage_quote: The group may be either a group name or a numeric group-ID (GID) prefixed with the ‘#’ character (e.g., ‘#0’ for GID 0).  When running a command as a GID, many shells require that the ‘#’ be escaped with a backslash (‘\’).  If no -u option is specified, the command will be run as the invoking user.  In either case, the primary group will be set to group.  The sudoers policy permits any of the target user's groups to be specified via the -g option as long as the -P option is not in use.

name: 013_preserve_env_list_repeatable.sh
expected: two --preserve-env= options are not rejected as a duplicate
manpage_quote: Indicates to the security policy that the user wishes to add the comma-separated list of environment variables to those preserved from the user's environment.  The security policy may return an error if the user does not have permission to preserve the environment.  This option may be specified multiple times.

name: 014_list_without_command_exit_zero.sh
exercises: flags: -l with no command exit value
expected: sudo -l (no command) exits 0 for an allowed+authenticated user
manpage_quote: If the -l option was specified without a command, sudo will exit with a value of 0 if the user is allowed to run sudo and they authenticated successfully (as required by the security policy).

name: 015_var_value_option_sets_env.sh
exercises: environment: VAR=value option reaches command environment
expected: VAR=value passed as an option sets that var for the command
manpage_quote: The sudoers policy subjects environment variables passed as options to the same restrictions as existing environment variables with one important difference.  If the setenv option is set in sudoers, the command to be run has the SETENV tag set or the command matched is ALL, the user may set variables that would otherwise be forbidden.

name: 016_login_shell_concatenates_command.sh
exercises: flags: -i login shell concatenates command + args
expected: sudo -i echo A B emits 'A B' on one line via shell -c
manpage_quote: If a command is specified, it is passed to the shell as a simple command using the -c option.  The command and any args are concatenated, separated by spaces, after escaping each character (including white space) with a backslash (‘\’) except for alphanumerics, underscores, hyphens, and dollar signs.

name: 017_shell_option_concatenates_command.sh
expected: sudo -s echo A B emits 'A B' on one line via SHELL -c
manpage_quote: Run the shell specified by the SHELL environment variable if it is set or the shell specified by the invoking user's password database entry.  If a command is specified, it is passed to the shell as a simple command using the -c option.  The command and any args are concatenated, separated by spaces, after escaping each character (including white space) with a backslash (‘\’) except for alphanumerics, underscores, hyphens, and dollar signs.
